newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India slides, Korea, Taiwan up with local.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India slides, Korea, Taiwan up with local.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts slid in London trade, while Korea and Taiwan rallied alongside gains on domestic markets.
"The GDR market traded down in line with the locals and it will not be surprising to see India open weaker tomorrow as kerb trading in Bombay was also weaker," said a broker.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed down 1.72 points, or 2.51 percent, at 66.80 points, with the premium over the local market at 12.89 percent compared with Friday's 14.29 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index lost 32.86 points, or 0.96 percent, to 3,389.49.
"We have seen some client selling of Indian GDRs, especially higher premium issues, but premiums now look much better value at 12-13 percent than 25-30 percent," said the broker.

The Capel Korea GDR Index rallied 1.55 points, or 1.67 percent, to 70.20, a premium of 48.37 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 24.23 points, or 3.49 percent, to 718.46.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended up 1.77 points, or 1.82 percent, at 99.02, a premium of 7.18 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index gained 100.12 points, or 1.40 percent, to close at 7,254.32.
